source.title: Alpaca against Vicuna: Using LLMs to Uncover Memorization of LLMs
source.authors: Aly M. Kassem; Omar Mahmoud; Niloofar Mireshghallah; Hyunwoo Kim; Y. Tsvetkov; Ye-Jin Choi; Sherif Saad; Santu Rana

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether optimized adversarial prompts elicit targeted Harry Potter material from an unlearned model, using a different attack and measure from the unlearning studies.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the Harry Potter unlearning case study. The paper's other memorization and extraction results do not test recovery from unlearning.
record.test_reason: In Section 6.2 the authors use LLM-optimized instruction prompts on the Harry Potter-unlearned Llama-2 (Eldan & Russinovich) and measure ROUGE-L overlap with 300 held passages. This compares a prompting-only attack against direct prefix prompting on the unlearned model, which bears on version E. The rest of the paper (memorization in instruction-tuned models, copyright, refusal, classifier) involves no unlearned model.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say optimized prompts elicited highly similar completions (23.6% vs 10.2% overlap) and that the unlearning technique is vulnerable to prompts that depart from the original training context.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies a prompt-optimization attack to a model unlearned by the method introduced in Who's Harry Potter?; it does not reproduce that unlearning procedure.
record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The unlearning case reports an aggregate overlap result without uncertainty or a pre-unlearning reference score; it does not assess preserved general ability or compare with a model that never saw the targeted material.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear directly on recovery from unlearning.

untested.parts: No forget accuracy near chance, general-ability check, or simple-attack failure is measured. The authors only cite that the original query test showed forgetting.
No activation ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Not tested: other languages, jailbreak templates, in-context information, comparison with the pre-unlearning model, and models beyond the single Harry Potter model.

missing.what: Prompt-to-suffix overlap (LCSP) for the Harry Potter prompts, needed to rule out the prompt itself supplying the overlapping text

record.verdict_notes: For loose context only, on other models and datasets: ROUGE-L on non-unlearned Llama-family Books passages is about .22-.25, and BookMIA non-members score 16.7. The 23.6% therefore sits near ordinary memorization-attack levels, but no direct reference exists. There is no uncertainty estimate and no human or semantic check that the completions contain Harry Potter-specific content.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether unlearning brings target accuracy near chance, preserves general ability, or whether simple attacks fail.
No fine-tuning or relearning data are used.
No activation direction is ablated, and the study does not analyze whether knowledge is blocked from access rather than deleted.

Tests optimized adversarial prompts on the Harry Potter case only; does not test other languages, jailbreaks, or in-context information, or compare recovery with the model's pre-unlearning performance.
No newer counter-method intended to resist recovery attacks is tested.

rows.subject: Llama-2 (unlearned model)
rows.operation_detail: Optimized prompts used to elicit completions resembling Harry Potter passages.
rows.locator: Section 6.2, Case Study: Eliciting Unlearned Harry Potter
rows.note: The paper describes the completions as highly similar, but does not report the unlearned model's pre-unlearning overlap or establish how much of the original knowledge was recovered.
rows.check: Subject should be the Llama-2 model unlearned by Eldan & Russinovich (size not stated in text). The measure is ROUGE-L, an approximate overlap, not exact recall. The baseline is prefix-suffix prompting of the same unlearned model, not the pre-unlearning model or a never-trained control, so how much was restored cannot be read. The default setting builds prompts from the full passage including the suffix, and prompt-suffix overlap (LCSP) is not reported for this case. Partial is kept: the overlap more than doubles (10.2% to 23.6%), but the extent of recovery is unestablished.

source_check.locator_found: Section 6.2, Results: '23.6% overlap compared to 10.2% using prefix-suffix prompts'
source_check.problem: None material. Section 6.2 says only 'overlap', but the paper's overlap metric throughout is ROUGE-L (Sec 2, 4.4). The Llama-2 size is not stated.

relationships.condition: Optimized paraphrase prompts, built with access to the full target passage, on the Harry Potter-unlearned Llama-2, 300 passages of 300 tokens
relationships.reason: Overlap rises from 10.2% to 23.6% ROUGE-L, so the unlearned model yields more text under rephrased prompts (r1). With no pre-unlearning reference and prompts derived from the passage, the amount restored is not shown.
relationships.display_finding: ROUGE-L overlap rose from 10.2% to 23.6%, but passage-derived prompts and the absence of a pre-unlearning reference leave the amount restored uncertain.

The reason's 'amount restored not shown' is an untested part and should not carry the label, but the label stands.

relation.reason: Section 6.2 reports its own result on prompting-only elicitation from the unlearned model.

tranche.reason: A different method (LLM-optimized instruction prompts) aimed at the same question: whether the WHP unlearning resists recovery. It does not reproduce the unlearning or its original measure.

source_check.notes: Only a short case study (Sec 6.2, one results sentence). There is no numeric pre-unlearning control, and the model size is not stated. The intro claims a '56.6% increase in privacy auditing over prefix-suffix (Eldan and Russinovich)', which does not match 6.2's 23.6% vs 10.2%. Use the Sec 6.2 figures.

statements.correction: Sec 6.2: optimized instruction prompts gave 23.6% overlap (ROUGE-L) vs 10.2% for prefix-suffix prompts. Model: HP-unlearned Llama-2 (Eldan & Russinovich). 300 passages of 300 tokens. No pre-unlearning figure is given.
statements.problem: No problem found for this study. 10.2% and 23.6% are in Sec 6.2 for the Eldan & Russinovich Llama-2. Prompts use full-passage access, the paper's default 'empirical upper bound' setting. The text gives no numeric pre-unlearning reference. The 10.2% is from prefix-suffix prompting, which the statement does not name.

statements.correction: If added: Sec 6.2, HP-unlearned Llama-2. Optimized prompts gave 23.6% overlap vs 10.2% for prefix-suffix prompts (prefix only). The optimized prompts were built with the full passage, using the suffix as ROUGE-L feedback. The unlearned model has no answer-blind optimized-prompt run.
statements.problem: The statement cites this study's r1 but never names the study or gives its numbers, so nothing about it can be checked. The citation dangles: either add the study or drop r1.
